title: Teaching Agents the "Principle", Not the "Reward"
abstract: arXiv:2611.07130v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reinforcement learning has achieved strong performance in many tasks by letting agents learn from nothing more than a reward signal. However, in more complex tasks, agents still struggle to learn good, generalizable policies, even with carefully designed rewards and abundant samples. We argue that this difficulty stems from the reward decoding burden: designers encode their knowledge of the desired behavior into rewards and penalties, and agents must infer this knowledge from long sequences of noisy scalars. To address this burden, we propose prescriptive policy learning (PPL), which directly teaches agents higher-level knowledge about the tasks, termed principles of behavior, such as how to maintain balance, how to accumulate energy, and how to land smoothly. translated_title: 教智能体学“原则”，而非“奖励”
translated_abstract: 强化学习通过让智能体仅从奖励信号中学习，已在许多任务中取得了出色的表现。然而，在更复杂的任务中，即使精心设计奖励并拥有充足的样本，智能体仍然难以学习到良好的、可泛化的策略。我们认为这一困难源于“奖励解码负担”：设计者将其关于期望行为的知识编码进奖励与惩罚之中，而智能体必须从冗长的含噪声标量序列中推断出这些知识。为解决这一负担，我们提出了规范性策略学习（PPL），它直接向智能体传授关于任务的高层知识，即“行为原则”，例如如何保持平衡、如何积累能量、如何平稳着陆。通过适当选择的关键量和参考值，PPL能够在每一步直接指示智能体是否遵循了这些原则以及遵循的程度。我们的实验表明……
tldr: 该论文提出规范性策略学习（PPL），通过直接向智能体传授“行为原则”等高层知识来替代仅靠奖励信号的学习方式，从而消除了“奖励解码负担”，帮助智能体在复杂任务中学到更可泛化的策略。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Prescriptive Policy Learning (PPL), which directly teaches agents high-level "principles of behavior" instead of relying solely on reward signals, thereby removing the reward decoding burden and enabling agents to learn generalizable policies in complex tasks.
